name: hCG
summary: A pregnancy hormone that acts like LH, prescribed to stimulate the testes in men with pituitary-related hypogonadism, for undescended testes, and to trigger ovulation.
what_it_is: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) is a protein hormone made by the placenta during pregnancy. Its action closely mirrors luteinizing hormone (LH), the pituitary hormone that signals the testes and ovaries, with a small amount of FSH-like activity. Products such as Pregnyl are purified from the urine of pregnant women and given by injection. Its label states it has not been shown to help treat obesity.

evidence.why: An FDA-approved prescription drug for male hypogonadism of pituitary origin, undescended testes and ovulation induction; evidence for its off-label use alongside testosterone comes from small, short studies.

status_us.label: FDA-approved prescription biologic; not for weight loss
status_us.note: Approved (for example as Pregnyl) for undescended testes, hypogonadism of pituitary origin in men and, after menotropins, ovulation induction. It has been regulated as a biologic since March 2020, which the compounding pharmacists' trade group says put it outside the reach of most compounding pharmacies; FDA has said over-the-counter and 'homeopathic' hCG diet products are illegal.

benefits.claim: Treats hypogonadism caused by a pituitary deficiency in selected men
Treats undescended testes in boys when there is no physical blockage, and, after menotropins, induces ovulation in some infertile women

Kept testosterone inside the testes near normal in 29 healthy men whose own LH and FSH were shut down by testosterone for 3 weeks; testosterone alone cut it by 94% (studied for off-label use alongside testosterone therapy)

risks.risk: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (sudden ovarian enlargement with fluid in the abdomen or chest) when used to induce ovulation
Multiple pregnancy (twins or more) with ovulation induction
Breast enlargement in men, fluid retention, headache, irritability, restlessness, depression and fatigue
Early puberty in boys treated for undescended testes
Blood clots in arteries, and allergic reactions including anaphylaxis
Very low-calorie 'hCG diets' can cause gallstones, electrolyte imbalance and irregular heartbeat; FDA says any weight loss comes from the diet, not the hCG

avoid_if: Prostate cancer or another androgen-dependent tumor
Heart or kidney disease, epilepsy, migraine or asthma (needs caution because of fluid retention)

before: Morning testosterone with LH and FSH, to confirm the cause of low testosterone
Semen analysis if fertility is the goal
during: Semen analysis if fertility is the goal
labs.why: The hCG label sets no lab schedule for men; tests like these show whether the testes are responding. Ovulation induction is managed by clinicians experienced in infertility, as the label requires.

studies.title: Low-Dose Human Chorionic Gonadotropin Maintains Intratesticular Testosterone in Normal Men with Testosterone-Induced Gonadotropin Suppression
studies.finding: Testosterone suppressed LH and FSH and cut testosterone inside the testes by 94% over 3 weeks; adding hCG limited the drop to 25% or less, or raised the level, depending on the amount. Sperm production was not measured.

studies.title: PREGNYL (chorionic gonadotropin for injection, USP): Prescribing Information
studies.people: Boys with undescended testes, men with pituitary-related hypogonadism and women undergoing ovulation induction
studies.finding: Lists the approved uses and states that hCG has not been demonstrated to be effective additional therapy for obesity.

ask_your_clinician: Is my low testosterone caused by a pituitary problem that hCG could treat?

notes_for_editor: The label cited is an April 2011 Pregnyl label from Drugs@FDA; newer versions may exist on DailyMed, and Novarel and Ovidrel (choriogonadotropin alfa, a recombinant form) were not checked. The label gives no frequencies for its side effects, so how_common is 'unknown' throughout. The compounding status rests on a post by the Alliance for Pharmacy Compounding (a trade group; the year is inferred from its URL), not an FDA document; round-1 notes say hCG is not among substances nominated for FDA's 503A bulks categories. The FDA hCG-diet warning dates from 2011. The hCG-with-testosterone evidence measures hormone levels inside the testes, not sperm counts or pregnancies.
